standard_prerequisites.name: Univalent type theory and supplied Cauchy-real recursion
standard_prerequisites.statement: Rational order, triangle inequality and positive epsilon refinements; dependent products and subset types; propositional truncation, function extensionality and univalence for mere propositions; the supplied joint Cauchy-real/closeness recursion and mere-property induction principles. Rounded code relations and their module properties are not allowed as inputs.

core_obligations: Design the outer space of rounded predicate families with one triangle law and the epsilon-shift relation whose separatedness follows by spending the roundedness margin.

Construct the rational and limit families by inner recursion into rounded propositions, with a second separated epsilon-shift relation, so that its preservation supplies exactly the missing membership condition for the outer codomain.
Supply the four rational/limit defining clauses and use both layers of Cauchy compatibility to establish all constructor cases of the right and left triangle laws.
difficulty_reason: The relation cannot be freely defined on representative Cauchy sequences and then quotiented. Even after the HIIT eliminators are supplied, the proof must build separated relation families by roundedness and nest two admissible recursions so their preservation conditions produce the desired metric module laws. This metric margin mechanism and rational/limit cases differ from the surreal order-code construction.

compared.difference: Migrates the unpublished old claim once; complete proof1170-1288 includes the old exported-text truncation after1240.

Both use HIIT elimination, but here separatedness follows from rounded epsilon margins, followed by rational/limit metric-module compatibility; the surreal target uses coupled strict/non-strict orders and dependent option transitivity. Neither follows from the other.
Contractibility of connected-truncated factorizations is a different construction and target.
Hypercubical manifold q-pres is a distinct cubical presentation result, not a Cauchy real metric-code theorem.
